findings.observation: The list and summary use legacy organisation storage context, and a raw client_id filter is applied without first converging the Client and invoice through approved-Site scope. Clientless or funder invoices leave an additional canonical Site/privacy boundary unresolved.

The per-page allocation aggregate is not constrained by canonical organisation, settlement Site, allocation type, or integrity provenance, while total_outstanding sums gross invoice totals rather than outstanding balances.
Invoice lines are eagerly returned to every finance.ar.view caller even though the frozen page uses them to prefill manager-only edit flows. Static ownership does not authorize that disclosure.

The manager-only invoice client picker asks UserSiteAccessService to accept reports.viewAny as a global fallback. That unrelated permission does not prove finance invoice authority or exact Site scope.

The action loads every application-context invoice into PHP for summary derivation while shared middleware also computes application-wide finance hub counts. Neither query path proves approved-Site privacy or efficient bounded aggregation.

Static links and filter callers, including a raw client_id query parameter, establish discoverability only. They do not prove caller authority, route reachability, runtime behavior, or privacy correctness.
Frozen tests do not establish the selected index action's foreign-Site, no-Site, forged client_id, view-only minimization, and global-Site positive contracts. No test was executed in this review.
Semantic review pinned seven widened packet files and five newly followed files. This bounded expansion does not rewrite the cohort's explicit incompleteness or grant correctness credit.
The selected Index render, existing Index owner, sibling Show owner, and static callers remain non-inheritable context. No page owner is added, reassigned, reopened, or re-credited.
